title: The Mystery of the Compass
text: Have you ever wondered why a compass always points North? What if I told you that an invisible force field is wrapping around our entire planet, and it is the same force that powers your favorite electronic gadgets? Let's unravel the mystery of electricity and magnetism!

content.title: Think About It!
content.instructions: Imagine you have a wire and a battery. If you connect them, does the wire get hot? Does it pull metallic objects? Predict what would happen if you brought a compass near the wire.

content.title: Magnetic Field Around a Wire
content.description: Notice how the magnetic field lines form circles around the wire when current flows.

title: The Magnetic Effect of Electric Current
text: When an electric current flows through a wire, it produces a magnetic field around it. This is called the magnetic effect of electric current. It was first observed by Hans Christian Ørsted.

content.question: What happens when electric current flows through a straight wire?
options: A magnetic field is created around the wire.

title: Reflection
text: Explain in your own words: If a straight wire creates a magnetic field, what would happen if we coil the wire into many loops?

title: Connecting the Dots
text: This very principle is what powers the electric motors in fans, washing machines, and even electric cars! It connects the invisible world of electrons to the physical motion we see every day.

content.title: Mini Challenge: Build Your Own Electromagnet
content.instructions: Take an iron nail, wrap a copper wire around it, and connect the ends to a battery. Try picking up some paper clips. You have just built a temporary magnet powered by electricity!

content.title: Teacher's Secret
content.text: Remember the Right-Hand Thumb Rule! If you point your right thumb in the direction of the current, your curled fingers will show the direction of the magnetic field.

content.title: Watch Out!
content.text: Don't confuse a permanent magnet with an electromagnet. An electromagnet only works when electricity is flowing!

title: The Heating Effect of Electric Current
text: Have you noticed your phone charger getting warm? When electric current flows through a conductor, some of the electrical energy is converted into heat. This is known as the heating effect.

content.title: Electrons Colliding
content.description: See how electrons bump into atoms as they move, creating friction and heat.

content.question: Which of the following devices works mainly on the heating effect of electric current?

content.title: Mastery Challenge: Home Audit
content.instructions: Look around your house and list 3 devices that use the heating effect and 3 that use the magnetic effect of electric current.
